title: Out of the river
told: a sakhi, a traditional story of Guru Nanak

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? has anyone ever guessed wrong about who you are?
options: then you’ll love this one. listen.
then you know the feeling. listen.
then listen to what sikhs hear a lot.

steps.line: Guru Nanak, a young man working in the town of Sultanpur, went to bathe in the river Bein one morning, as he always did.
steps.label: a traditional story

steps.line: He didn’t come out. The town searched the banks for three days.

steps.q: On the third day he comes back. What do you think his first words are?
o: There is no Hindu, there is no Muslim
I saw a vision of heaven
steps.why: Na ko Hindu, na Musalman. In the janamsakhis this is the first thing he says once he speaks again, and the Sikh path grows from it.

steps.line: On the third day he walked out of the water and said: there is no Hindu, there is no Muslim.

steps.q: Sikhs hear a lot in that line. Which fits it best?
o: Beneath the labels, everyone is made by the one God
Hindus and Muslims should merge into one new religion
He was giving up faith altogether
steps.why: Many hear: under the labels, everyone is made by the one. Some also hear a challenge: few truly live up to the name they carry.

steps.line: The town’s governor and its judge, the qazi, heard about it. Then come and pray with us, they said.

steps.q: In the mosque, everyone bows in prayer. What do you think Nanak does?
steps.why: He stood while they bowed, and afterwards they demanded to know why. His answer turned the question back on them.

steps.line: At prayer time Nanak stood with them in the mosque, but didn’t bow. Afterwards they asked him why.
Your mind wasn’t here, he told the qazi gently. It was at home with your new foal. The qazi went quiet. It was true.
steps.label: a traditional story

steps.q: You’re the qazi, caught thinking about your foal in the middle of prayer. Why might you go quiet instead of angry?
o: Nanak had named exactly what was true
steps.why: In the sakhi, the qazi admits it. Many tellings say the governor bowed to Nanak after that, struck by how plainly he saw.

steps.line: Sikh means a learner. Guru Nanak’s path grew into a faith of its own. Not Hindu, not Muslim, and it puts neither down.
steps.label: today

steps.q: Sikh means learner. Who does a Sikh learn from?
o: Their own reading, with no teacher
The Guru, and through the Guru, God
steps.why: Sikh comes from Sanskrit shishya, student. Sikhs learn from the ten Gurus and now the Guru Granth Sahib, the scripture they treat as a living Guru.

say: here’s what i love. nanak’s first words weren’t against anyone. they were an invitation to look underneath the labels.
the word sikh means learner. sikhs walk a path of their own, and it needs nobody else’s faith put down.

steps.q: From the mosque story, what was Nanak really saying about prayer?
o: Bowing in prayer is a mistake
Prayer counts when the heart is really there
Prayer is best done alone, at home
steps.why: He didn’t mock their prayer or their bowing. He pointed to the real thing: a heart that is actually present.

today.say: if someone asks you about sikhs this week, you have the plain answer now: a learner, on a path of its own. try saying it once, out loud or just to yourself.
options: a learner, on a path of its own. that’s it.

card.keepWhy: He walked out of the river with one line.

Sakhi of Guru Nanak at prayer with Nawab Daulat Khan and the qazi (the qazi’s mind on his newborn foal)
